summary: ING sits clearly with the traditional banks on this measured comparison (position score 0.17), separated from peers mainly by a very high volume of quoted figures, a large opening image and stronger youth targeting. Its page craft is otherwise at or above the field — clarity of the offer, campaign structure completeness, opening attention and mobile-first signals all score above the peer mean — but calls to action are the one feature where ING falls clearly below peers (0.5 against 5.65). The evidence is design measurement only: no clicks, conversions or sales are in the data, the pages span four product families and two languages, and everything is valid only for the 2026-09-21 capture.

recommendations.title: Rebuild the opening so the promise and action sit beside the image
recommendations.finding: The size of the opening image measures 0.53 at ING against a peer mean of 0.26, about 1.1 standard deviations above the field. ING also opens with something that stops the reader (0.5 against 0.17) and its clarity of the offer is above peers (4.0 against 3.5), so the attention and the message exist — but the image is consuming the space where the action would sit.
recommendations.recommendation: Cap the opening image so the headline promise, the qualifying line and the primary call to action are all visible without scrolling, and let the image support rather than dominate the first screen. Test this on the campaign pages where the opening image is largest.

recommendations.title: Add the missing calls to action at every decision point
recommendations.finding: Calls to action measures 0.5 at ING against a peer mean of 5.65 — around one standard deviation below the field, and the only feature in the comparison where ING is clearly behind. Campaign structure completeness is already slightly above peers (3.5 against 3.0), so the attention, interest and desire blocks are built but the action block is not.
recommendations.recommendation: Insert repeated, identically worded calls to action: one in the first screen, one after each proof block, and one at the end of the page, plus a persistent mobile action. Keep the wording and destination consistent so the same next step is offered throughout.

recommendations.title: State the conditions of any “free” claim in the same block
recommendations.finding: “Free” with conditions attached scores 0.5 at ING against a peer mean of 0.15, close to one standard deviation above the field. ING's clarity of the offer is good (4.0 against 3.5), so this is a disclosure placement issue rather than a wording issue: the qualifier exists but is separated from the claim.
recommendations.recommendation: For every “free” or zero-cost claim, place the qualifying conditions directly beneath the claim in the same visual block, in plain language and at readable size, rather than in a footnote or a link. Apply it consistently across the offers that carry a condition.

recommendations.title: Cut the number of figures quoted on the page
recommendations.finding: Figures and percentages quoted is ING's single largest deviation from the field: 25.5 against a peer mean of 12.15, about 1.6 standard deviations above. Pages that quote this many numbers make the reader choose between claims instead of following one.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep only the two or three numbers that directly support the page's main promise, move the rest into a clearly labelled details table or an expandable section, and check that no two blocks on the same page quote competing numbers for the same thing.

recommendations.title: Shorten the long campaign pages
recommendations.finding: Page length measures 9,465 pixels at ING against a peer mean of 6,397, about 0.9 standard deviations above. ING's campaign structure is already complete (3.5 against 3.0), so the extra length is not adding structure — it is repeating it.
recommendations.recommendation: Audit the longest pages block by block, merge duplicated proof sections, and move secondary detail such as full condition lists into expandable panels. Aim to bring the page length closer to the peer mean without dropping any of the structure that already scores above average.

recommendations.title: Test a rate-led framing on the savings and credit pages
recommendations.finding: The analysis places ING clearly with the traditional banks (position score 0.17). Within that cluster a rate is shown in 0.0 of cases while challenger pages show one in 0.5 of cases, and subscription-style framing is absent from the traditional cluster (0.0) against 0.5 for challengers. This is a style-level observation, not evidence about performance.
recommendations.recommendation: Pilot a version of the savings and credit campaign pages that puts the headline rate, with its conditions, in the first screen, and compare it against the current framing in a controlled test on ING's own traffic.

recommendations.title: Extend the mobile-first treatment into the long-form sections
recommendations.finding: Designed mobile-first scores 1.0 at ING against a peer mean of 0.5 — one of ING's clearest strengths, and level with the challenger cluster (1.0) versus 0.4 for the traditional cluster. The same pages are also long (9,465 pixels against 6,397) and carry few calls to action (0.5 against 5.65), which are exactly the conditions where a mobile-first layout stops helping.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the mobile-first approach and push it into the sections that are currently longest: shorten or collapse text-heavy blocks on small screens, and make sure the repeated calls to action remain reachable without excessive scrolling on a phone.

recommendations.title: Pilot a more image-led, less uniformly bright page treatment
recommendations.finding: ING's position sits with the traditional cluster, where page brightness averages 0.86 against 0.56 for challengers and share of the page that is imagery averages 0.10 against 0.34. These are cluster-level averages with large effects, but ING's own value on both is not among the measured gaps and no performance data exists in this project.
recommendations.recommendation: On one campaign page, test a variant that gives more of the mid-page to imagery and lowers the overall brightness of the background, keeping the same copy and the same calls to action, so the styling change can be read on its own.
